detailed_syllabus.topic: Safety rules and regulations in Auto body repairs and spray painting

subtopics.content: Definition of safety rules and regulations in auto body repairs and spray painting
List of rules and regulations and their importance
List of safety tools and equipment/machines for auto body repairs
Auto body dressing code: personal protective equipment (nose mask, goggles, boots, ear defender, etc)
Sources of accident (human factors, machinery/equipment and workshop keeping) and their preventions

Factory acts on safety rules and regulations: 1984 amended resource conservation recovery act, environmental protection agency regulations and hazardous waste collection and recycling (solvent recovery system)

practical: 1:3:1 Identification of safety tools and equipment and demonstration of their usage
1:4:1 Identification of dress code and protective equipment and demonstration of their usage
1:5:1 Identification of containers for hazardous waste
1:5:2 Demonstration of horse play
1:5:3 Report faulty machines/equipment
1:5:4 Demonstration of workshop keeping e.g. cleaning oil and water from the floor with saw dust and dry sand

subtopics.content: Types of hand tools (hammers, dollies, spanner, files, ratchets, body spoons, etc) and their uses
Types and uses of power tools and equipment/machines (drilling machine, body jack, sanders, air compressor, shaping machines, cutting machine, etc)
Advantages and disadvantages of machines
Uses of machines and safety precautions
Spray painting tools and equipment (scrapers, brushes, funnels, paint pots, spray gun, spray body filters, air compressor, oven, spray boot, etc)

subsections.subsection: (d) Care and maintenance of tools and equipment

subtopics.content: Definition of maintenance and types – predictive, preventive and corrective
Manufacturer’s maintenance guide
Maintenance of tools and equipment

practical: 2:1:1 Identification of hand tools and equipment
2:2:1 Identification and demonstration of the use of power tools
2:4:1 Demonstration of the use of machine
2:5:1 Identification of spray painting tools, equipment and their uses
2:8:1 Dismantling and assembly of a spray gun
2:8:2 Cleaning of tools and equipment

detailed_syllabus.topic: Materials for auto-body repairs and spray painting

subtopics.content: Types of body filler - plastic filler; fibreglass fillers; body solder; 30/70 and 40/60
Type of body abrasives e.g. sand papers (wet and dry); Sanding disc
Type of sealers e.g. rubber sealers, seam sealers, undercoating, etc
Rivet pins e.g. pop and solid rivets
Types of paints – Enamel paints and lacquers. Under coats: surface primer, putty/body filler, sealers. Top coats: lacquers and enamel paints
Manufactures paint guide: paint formula, paint mixing equipment, custom-mix basecolours, paint labels, colour charts

practical: 3:1:1 Identification of body fillers
3:2:1 Identification of body abrasives
3:4:1 Demonstration of the use of rivet gun
3:5:1 Identification of paints by use of thinner
3:5:2 Demonstration of the use of under coats
3:5:3 Demonstration of those of top coats
3:6:1 Demonstration of how to mix paints
3:6:2 Identification of colours using colour charts

subtopics.content: Ferrous and non ferrous metals – mild steel, cast iron, aluminium, brass, etc
Properties of metals – fusibility, malleability, ductility, weldability, etc
Uses of metals on Auto bodies

practical: 4:1:1 Identification of ferrous and non-ferrous metals
4:1:2 Demonstration of properties of metals

subtopics.content: Definition of heat treatment
Types and process of heat treatment e.g. hardening, annealing, normalizing, case-hardening and tempering
Importance of heat treatment

practical: 5:2:1 Demonstration of heat treatment processes

subtopics.content: Definition of oxy-acetylene welding
Safety precautions
Oxy-acetylene welding equipment
Types of oxy-acetylene gas used e.g. (high and low pressure system)
Installations of welding equipment
Welding nozzles
Defects of oxy-acetylene welding – slag inclusion, porosity, crack, lack of penetration, etc and their remedies

practical: 6:3:1 Identification of equipment
6:4:1 Demonstration of how to use high and low pressure system
6:5:1 Demonstration of how to assemble welding equipment
6:6:1 Demonstration of how to install welding equipment
6:7:1 Identification of weld defects

subtopics.content: Types of auto body (i) integral body; (ii) composite body

Basic methods of straightening auto body: aligning the metal with power jack, pulling the metal with sledge hammer, using pre-bar, pulling the metal with pull taps. Heat-shrinking the metal to bring the metal back to its original shape
Tools used in minor repairs- hammers, hand dollies, spoons, spanners, screw drivers, etc
Major body sections e.g. front engine compartment, passenger section, rear section
Basic alignment principle
Quarter panel cutting
Light weight panels
Damaged vehicle alignment

practical: 7:1:1 Identification of integral and composite bodies
7:2:1 Identification of auto-body repair tools
7:2:2 Identification of heat shrinking tools
7:3:1 Demonstration of how to use the tools in carrying out minor repairs
7:4:1 Identification of major body sections
7:6:1 Identification of quarter panel and demonstration of how to cut it
7:7:1 Repair and aligning of body sections

subtopics.content: Steps involved in aluminum panel repair
Repair and alignment of damaged aluminum panel
Aluminum deck lid repair

practical: 8:2:1 Demonstration of how to repair and align aluminum panel
8:3:1 Aluminum deck lid repair procedure

subtopics.content: Precautions while working with plastics
Types of plastic resins (thermosetting and thermoplastic)
Repair of plastic parts by melting
Introduction to glass fibre panel repair

practical: 9:2:1 Identification of plastics
9:3:1 Demonstration of how to repair plastics parts by melting

subtopics.content: Spray gun – pressure feed gun, siphon and gravity gun
Spray gun parts – air cap, fluid needle, air valve, trigger gun, body, cup, etc
Precautions in the use of spray gun
Manufacturer’s maintenance guide
Preparation of surfaces for spray painting
Paints used on auto bodies: cellulose synthetic paint, enamel paint, acrylic, metallic paints, etc
Importance of manufacturer’s paint code
Special paints and their importance
Variable agents (flakes and pigments)
Metallic spray techniques (wet and dry spray)
